sources.entry: time-machine - Travel through time in your tests by mocking the current time at the C level.

summary.one_liner: time-machine is a Python testing library that mocks the current time so tests can run as if at a chosen date or time.
summary.what_it_does: The README shows a decorator, time_machine.travel(), that takes a datetime (with optional timezone) and makes code calling the current date or time behave as if that moment is now within the decorated test. The example uses a timezone-aware datetime and checks that dt.date.today() returns the chosen date. The README's listing in vinta/awesome-python describes it as mocking the current time at the C level. The README given here is truncated: it stops at a "Documentation" heading with a link to the full docs, so further features are not visible in this text.
use_cases: write tests that depend on a specific date
check behavior at a past or future time in unit tests
freeze or simulate the current time in pytest-style tests
notable: Decorator-based time travel via time_machine.travel() with datetime input
Mocks current time at the C level, per the awesome-python listing
Works with timezone-aware datetimes such as zoneinfo.ZoneInfo
caveats: README provided is truncated; installation and full API details are only in the external documentation it links to
Platform or Python version support is not stated in the provided README text
